text.title: Django Services Layer Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree mapping observable signals to a rule from content/01-core-rules.xml. The skip-this-methodology and run-the-checklist branches are always reachable.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the change perform writes across ≥2 models, trigger side effects, or carry logic reused by more than one caller?

conclusion.verdict: skip — explicit handlers already in use
block — pass primitives, not the request
block — route DB writes through services
make args kw-only and fully typed
validate with a serializer or pydantic at the boundary
approve — walk the procedure and run the validator

text.example: View POST /orders/ accepts payload, creates Order + OrderLine + AuditLog, then sends confirmation email. Extract into order_create(*, user_id: int, items: list[dict], notes: str | None = None) -> Order in apps.orders.services. Wrap in @transaction.atomic because 3 writes. Replace send_email.delay(order.id) with transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_email.delay(order.id)). View becomes a 4-line dispatch; import-linter confirms no HTTP import in services and no ORM mutation outside them → all_gates_green=true → approve.
